title: Local constraints are where the future arrives
summary: A qualitative map built from Published global, utility, facility, workforce, infrastructure, permit, and development-pipeline records, showing how compute, chips, and housing plans become local outcomes only through receiving systems with open evidence gaps.
map_question: Which Published records show frontier demand entering local receiving systems, and which dependencies still lack project-level evidence?
interpretation_boundary: This map connects Published FTFN records to explicit evidence gaps. It does not prove local readiness, project viability, sufficient facility capacity, permit completion, housing delivery, or operating outcomes.

nodes.label: AI and data-centre electricity demand
nodes.note: Global growth creates a grid bottleneck watch, but it is not a local load forecast or a finding of available service.

nodes.label: U.S. Southwest Chip Corridor
nodes.note: A receiving system where compute and semiconductor investment meets power, water, labor, permitting, suppliers, and infrastructure.

nodes.label: Conditional large-load service
nodes.note: SRP's tariff creates concrete forecasting, billing, agreement, and infrastructure conditions without proving capacity at a named site.

nodes.label: Fab 3 topping-out milestone
nodes.note: The structural milestone is stronger than an investment announcement and remains upstream of occupancy, equipment qualification, and production.

nodes.label: Phoenix workforce baseline
nodes.note: Official metropolitan employment and wage data establish a local baseline without proving semiconductor workforce sufficiency.

nodes.label: Project-level power capacity
nodes.note: Named service agreements, substations, transmission, interconnection, precise points of delivery, and reliability evidence remain incomplete.

nodes.label: Project-level water and wastewater capacity
nodes.note: Provider, facility-demand, reuse, discharge, construction, commissioning, and performance evidence remain incomplete.

nodes.label: Semiconductor workforce outcomes
nodes.note: Occupation, vacancy, completion, placement, retention, supplier, and employer-demand evidence is still needed.

nodes.label: Ontario Real Estate
nodes.note: A receiving system where targets, approvals, infrastructure, capital, permits, starts, completions, and occupancy determine delivery.

nodes.label: Toronto development pipeline
nodes.note: The citywide pipeline establishes large potential supply and explicitly preserves uncertainty between proposal, approval, permit, construction, and completion.

nodes.label: Toronto Water capital delivery
nodes.note: The adopted capital plan adds infrastructure and reserve context without establishing servicing capacity for a named development.

nodes.label: Building-permit intentions
nodes.note: Monthly permit values and authorized dwellings indicate intentions, not starts, completions, occupancy, or delivered supply.

nodes.label: Housing target conversion
nodes.note: Municipal servicing, approvals, infrastructure capacity, construction, and delivery evidence remain unresolved.

nodes.label: Permit-to-completion conversion
nodes.note: Project-level starts, completions, cancellations, financing, and local absorption evidence is still needed.

links.note: Global compute and data-centre demand matters locally only where power, water, land, labor, and permitting systems can absorb it.
The SRP tariff supplies a named service-condition record for large new loads in part of the corridor.
The City record supplies a physical construction milestone for a named Phoenix semiconductor facility.
BLS supplies a comparable Phoenix-area labor baseline beneath company and training-program claims.
A tariff states conditions for service; it does not identify available capacity, a precise point of delivery, or an executed agreement for a named project.
The structural milestone does not establish completed reclaimed-water or wastewater capacity, commissioning, or performance.
Metropolitan estimates do not resolve employer-specific demand, training completion, placement, retention, or supplier workforce needs.
The City pipeline supplies a stage-aware local baseline for proposed, approved, permitting, and completed units.
The adopted water capital plan makes infrastructure delivery and reserve pressure visible at city scale.
The monthly permits release adds current intentions data while preserving the distinction from delivered supply.
The pipeline identifies potential and stage counts, but project-level servicing, financing, start, and completion evidence remains incomplete.
A citywide capital plan does not establish accepted servicing capacity or completed infrastructure for a named development.
Permit intentions require project-level starts, completions, cancellations, financing, and occupancy evidence.

what_this_map_supports: Published records can show frontier demand entering local utility, construction, workforce, infrastructure, planning, and permit systems.
Named local records are more informative than broad state or provincial context while still leaving project-level gaps open.
A physical facility milestone, service tariff, workforce baseline, capital plan, pipeline count, and permit release describe different conversion stages.
The dependency-stack thesis can be represented without a readiness ranking or numeric score.
what_this_map_does_not_prove: It does not prove local readiness for semiconductor, AI, advanced-packaging, or housing outcomes.
It does not establish project-level power, water, workforce, servicing, financing, permit conversion, occupancy, or operating sufficiency.
It does not turn a topping-out event, tariff, capital plan, pipeline, or permit release into completed capacity or delivered outcomes.
It does not rank local systems or create a 42/59 score.
next_records_needed: Named utility service agreements, substations, transmission, interconnection, precise-point-of-delivery, and reliability records for gap-001.
Provider and facility water, wastewater, reuse, discharge, construction, commissioning, and performance records for gap-002.
Semiconductor occupation, vacancy, training completion, placement, retention, supplier, and employer-demand records for gap-003.
Municipal servicing, infrastructure, approval-timeline, financing, start, completion, and occupancy records for gap-004.
Geography- and project-specific permit, start, completion, cancellation, financing, and absorption records for gap-005.
